What I do

Two things, done properly

The focus stays narrow on purpose. These are the two kinds of work that consistently repay bringing in a specialist.

01

ERP order automation from marketplaces

When orders start in one system and get typed into another, you pay for the same work twice and inherit every typo along the way. I design and build the integration properly, so an order placed on Amazon or Best Buy is created in your ERP automatically, validated, and ready to fulfil.

Exceptions are flagged and routed for review. They do not sit in somebody’s inbox, and nothing depends on someone remembering to check.

  • Amazon and Best Buy, straight into Dynamics 365 F&O
  • Built on Celigo, connected to the tools you already have
  • No re-typing, no copy and paste, no missed orders
02

Support team into a customer experience team

Most support teams spend the day answering the same questions. I rebuild that operation end to end: Intercom and Fin AI configured so routine questions are resolved right away, workflows cleaned up, and your team free to spend its time on the conversations that actually need a person.

You decide how much the AI resolves. Some teams want a lot handled, some want a little. We set it where you are comfortable, prove it, and turn it up over time.

  • Intercom and Fin AI, set up end to end
  • Chat and voice now, email next
  • You set how much the AI handles

How it works

Here’s how working with me goes

STEP 1

Book a call

You tell me about your team and where the manual work is piling up. Most companies have a lot of moving pieces to wrangle, and this call is where we sort out which piece to pull first. If I don’t think I can help, I’ll tell you that too.

STEP 2

Start with one project

We pick the one process costing you the most time, and I scope it out before any work starts. Small first project, on purpose. Prove it works, then decide if there’s a second one worth doing.

STEP 3

I build it, you keep it

I build the automation in your tools, test it with your team, and hand it over with notes on how it works. It’s yours. Your team can run it without me.

Not sure which process is costing you the most? That’s fine. That’s most of the first call.

Who it’s for

Small teams where everybody wears a lot of hats

A good fit looks like this

  • A company of about 50 people or fewer, where the same few people do a bit of everything
  • An operations or customer experience leader who can see the manual work stacking up
  • Orders coming in from marketplaces that still get handled by hand
  • A support team answering the same questions all day
  • Tools that don’t talk to each other, like a CRM over here and an ERP over there

Where this comes up most

Consumer brands that sell on marketplaces, small SaaS companies with a real support load, clinics, trades and home services, hospitality and events, professional services, and membership organizations.

If your business isn’t on that list but the busywork sounds familiar, reach out anyway. Repetition looks pretty much the same everywhere.

Questions

Fair questions, straight answers

What happens on the first call?+

You tell me where the manual work is piling up. I ask about your team and your tools. Then I’ll tell you what I’d automate first and whether I think it’s worth your money. And yes, I’m pitching you. That’s what the call is. It’s also a real conversation, and if it’s not a fit, I’ll say so.

Do I need to buy new software?+

Probably not. I build in the tools you already have: Intercom, Celigo, the Microsoft stack, your CRM, your ERP. If I think a tool change is actually worth it, I’ll show you why before you spend anything.

How much will the AI resolve in support?+

As much as you want it to. We start where you are comfortable, measure how it performs, and adjust from there. The level is always your call, and it can change over time. The case study page shows how that played out in practice on a documented engagement.

How big is a first project?+

Small. One process, scoped out before we start. If it saves the time it’s supposed to, we can talk about a second one.

Who actually does the work?+

Me. LEVER is my practice, so the person on your first call is the person who builds it.

I’m not in Utah. Does that matter?+

No. I’m in St. George, Utah, and most of this work happens inside your systems either way. A call is a call.

Context

The work, in full

At Wilson Connectivity I manage customer experience. A big part of that role has been building automations across the operation: integrations between marketplaces and the ERP, Intercom and Fin AI for support, and reports that build themselves. The three projects below are that work, broken down the way I would break down any engagement: the problem, what was built, and the result.

Celigo, Integration

Marketplace orders going straight into the ERP

The problem. Wilson sells through marketplaces like Amazon and Best Buy. Those orders were getting processed into the ERP by hand. Slow, boring, and easy to mess up.

What I built. An integration built with Celigo that takes marketplace orders and processes them automatically into Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations. A sale on Amazon becomes an order in the system without anyone re-typing it. Errors get flagged and handled instead of sitting in somebody’s inbox.

The result. That manual step is just gone. It is one of the automations that adds up to upwards of $150,000 in annual spend saved at Wilson.

Amazon and Best Buy, straight into Dynamics 365 F&O
marketplace sales processed automatically into the ERP
$150,000+
in annual spend saved across the automations built at Wilson
Intercom, Fin AI

Automating about 60% of support questions at weBoost

The problem. weBoost is Wilson’s consumer brand. The support team was answering the same questions over and over, on chat, on the phone, in email. Good people spending their whole day on repeat.

What I built. I implemented Intercom as the support platform and rolled out Fin AI, chat first, then voice, with email next in line. I also cleaned up a lot of the internal processes around it, which made the team’s day to day a lot simpler.

The result. About 60% of all inquiries get handled automatically now. Customers get faster answers, and it improved things for the team too, not just the customers.

Microsoft stack, Reporting

Internal reports that send themselves

What I built. Recurring internal reports that put themselves together and go out on schedule. Set it up once, and it just runs.

The result. Nobody has to remember to make them, and nobody spends a morning copying numbers into a deck.
